row.entry: Month of the base map version used.
Unique identifier for a city. Typically, the FIPS code.
Unique identifier for a county. Typically, the FIPS code or Canadian census subdivision CSDUID from StatCan.
User input date ranges for filtering. Array of objects containing DateFrom (date) and DateTo (date).
Integers representing each week day. 1 = Sunday, 2 = Monday, etc.
The distance traveled (in kilometers or miles).
The amount of time spent at a destination (in minutes).
The fuel types that you can select for your analyses. Options include diesel, electric, flexible, gasoline, hybrid, other, and unknown. See Fuel Types to read a description of each option.
The geospatial bounds of an area of interest.
The vehicle is running and is stationary

entry.p: Describes the idle duration of a vehicle This includes the following API terms:

dlentry.dd: The average idle duration during the stop

Idle duration at the stop location before turning off ignition for the user-provided percentiles. Percentiles will only be provided if there are deemed sufficient records to calculate requested percentiles.
The median idle duration before turning off ignition at the stop location (minutes).
The standard deviation of idle duration before turning off ignition at the stop location (minutes).

row.entry: The percentage of journeys by industry as defined by the primary NAICS code. The primary NAICS code is determined by the fleet operating the vehicle that is contributing to the data.
Whether the user specified to compute things in metric (TRUE) or imperial (FALSE) units.
The state ISO code of the returned zone.
Metrics broken out by industry NAICS code.
Metrics broken out by vehicle class.
Metrics broken out by vehicle vocation.
Integers representing industry IDs. See the Industry table for specific industry codes.
The most up-to-date day of OSM when the base map used was generated.
Array of strings representing the different road types for which you want data. An empty array means all road types.
A unique identifier for the road segment which can be obtained from the API to get segment IDs can be found in the API Guide.

entry.p: Describes the stop duration of a vehicle. This includes the following API terms:

dlentry.dd: The maximum and minimum duration of the stop to be included in your analysis.
The standard deviation of stop duration (in minutes).
Stop duration (in minutes) for user provided percentiles. Percentiles will only be provided if there are deemed sufficient records to calculate requested percentiles.

row.entry: User input time range for filtering. Object containing TimeFrom (time) and TimeTo (time).

entry.p: The vehicle speed when traveling between areas of interest (in kph or mph). Travel speed is calculated as the total distance traveled divided by the duration it takes to travel the distance (including idling time). This includes the following API terms:

dlentry.dd: The average travel speed (km/h or mph) for journeys. Travel speed is calculated as the total distance divided by the journey duration.
The median travel speed (km/h or mph) for journeys. Travel speed is calculated as the total distance divided by the journey duration.
The standard deviation of travel speed (km/h or mph) for journeys. Travel speed is calculated as the total distance divided by the journey duration.

row.entry: The time taken to travel between areas of interest, including any time stopped (in kph or mph).
When a vehicle starts moving until it stops with ignition turned off, or idles for at least 3 minutes, 20 seconds.
The percentage of journeys by vehicle class as defined by GVWR.
An array of vehicle class objects where each object contains VehicleType and WeightClass.
User input vehicle class scheme ID.
The number of unique vehicles contributing to the stop count.
The percentage of journeys by vocation.
The purpose (or job) of the vehicle. A patented machine learning algorithm determines this based on the observed driving pattern of each vehicle.
A collection of nodes defined by OpenStreetMap.
Description of the zone when available, such as road name.
A unique identifier for the zone; can be any string.
An enclosed area on the map, created by a user, used to categorize a landmark or area of interest.
Defines the type zone. Utilized to classify standard zones (e.g. county, city), custom zones and segments.
